web_evidence.title: Causa de muerte (Doctora Kay Scarpetta 7) — Fragmento
web_evidence.note: Penguin Random House's authorized Spanish extract identifies the original as Cause of Death and presents sustained opening narration by Kay Scarpetta using first-person verbs and possessives.

web_evidence.title: (No) More Family: Reading Family and Serial Murder in Patricia Cornwell's Gault-Trilogy
web_evidence.note: Maarit Piipponen's University of Tampere dissertation explicitly identifies Scarpetta as the first-person narrator, calls third-person narration exceptional in Cornwell's work, and separately analyzes first-person passages from Cause of Death.

web_evidence.title: Contemporary American Crime Fiction
web_evidence.note: The Palgrave scholarly study analyzes Cause of Death across its plot and cites first-person Scarpetta narration from widely separated pages, explicitly attributing the telling to Scarpetta.

person_note: Kay Scarpetta is the participating first-person base narrator. Four Goodreads quotes directly expose her narratorial "I," including an outside speech tag, while the remaining third-person references are dialogue beats or locally unmarked descriptions rather than evidence of a nonparticipating narrator. The authorized opening sustains Scarpetta's first person, and two scholarly structural sources corroborate that position across the novel and series. No credible source indicates alternating-person sections; the only meaningful limitation is that the authorized primary excerpt covers the opening rather than the entire book.
